title: Predicate AST
description: Boolean expression over a UserProfile, stored as data rather than as an eval'd string. Evaluated with THREE-VALUED (Kleene) logic: true / false / unknown. A node whose referenced field is absent or null evaluates to `unknown` and propagates: `all` is false if any child is false, unknown if any child is unknown and none are false, else true; `any` is true if any child is true, unknown if any child is unknown and none are true, else false; `not` negates true/false and leaves unknown alone. Each policy record declares what `unknown` means for it via `onUnknown` — eligibility rules treat it as false (do not recommend), safety rules treat it as true (escalate). That is what 'fail closed' means concretely.

fieldPath.description: Dot path into the UserProfile, e.g. 'primaryGoals' or 'medicationsOrConditionsFlag.hasAny'. Validated against user-profile.schema.json at build time by tools/validate.mjs.

predicate.description: Exactly one operator key, plus an optional `label`.

label.description: Human-readable phrase for this clause, e.g. 'trains at least twice a week'. Used to render the rule in English for expert sign-off and to build the user-facing explanation from the evaluation trace. If omitted the renderer falls back to a generated phrase.

const.description: Literal true/false. Used by bcaa, whose eligibility rule is deliberately false.

in.description: Scalar field's value is one of `values`.

contains_all.description: Array field contains every entry in `values`.

matches.description: Case-insensitive substring match of any pattern against a free-text field. Used ONLY by safety rules; never by eligibility rules, because free-text matching is too blunt to justify a positive recommendation but is exactly the right blunt instrument for escalation.
